applicability: Valid for 1 to 8 integer operands each in [-10,20] and exactly len(operands)-1 operators drawn from '+','-','*'. Booleans are rejected as non-integers. Malformed inputs (wrong types, wrong operator count, out-of-range operands, unknown keys) raise ValueError. Returns the count of distinct values over all full parenthesizations preserving operand and operator order. Does not handle other operators, reordering, or larger operand counts.
description: Interval dynamic programming over the fixed operand/operator sequence. For each contiguous subexpression dp[i][j] we store the set of all distinct integer values reachable by fully parenthesizing operands i..j. Base case dp[i][i]={operands[i]}. For each length and split point k, combine every value from dp[i][k] with every value from dp[k+1][j] using operators[k], inserting into dp[i][j]. The answer is the cardinality of dp[0][n-1]. Sets collapse duplicates so each distinct value counts once. Python arbitrary-precision integers avoid overflow. Uncertainty: none in the mathematical condition; runtime is bounded because n<=8 and per-interval value sets are at most the number of parenthesizations (Catalan(7)=429), so the O(n^3 * S^2) combination is small.
